resources.string: Every CarPlay and Android Auto option, inside its category
Exact values are set under Show advanced.
Start CarPlay or Android Auto when a paired phone’s Bluetooth connects
Start as soon as a phone is connected with a USB cable
Open CarLink when the head unit turns on and connect the last phone
You disconnected, so CarLink won’t reconnect on its own until you connect again.
For rooted stereos. Allows everything setup asks for without popups, and keeps Wi-Fi in low-latency mode while a phone is connected. Your root manager asks once.
Root is not available or was refused, so Root mode stays off.
When a wireless connection needs the stereo\'s hotspot and it is off, CarLink tries to switch it on. Needs \"Modify system settings\" for CarLink; some stereos only allow it with debugging approved.
Wireless through the stereo\'s Bluetooth module (experimental)

This stereo\'s Bluetooth is a separate module. Wireless Android Auto and CarPlay reach your phone through it; on by default. Turn off if wireless misbehaves on this stereo; USB still works. Applies from the next connection.
First disable the stereo\'s own “Car Link” app (com.syu.carlink) in Android Settings › Apps.
How the phone and the car share Wi-Fi

Picks the best path before each connection: same Wi-Fi, then the car hotspot, then Wi-Fi Direct. With Android Auto it also connects through the phone’s head unit server when it is on and both are on one network.
Phone and car on one router, the fastest path. Needs the Wi-Fi password once.
The phone joins the Wi-Fi hotspot the car creates. Works with every phone.
A direct link between phone and car. No network needed.
Android Auto backup: this screen joins the phone\'s hotspot. Turn on Start head unit server on the phone.
Bluetooth starts the connection (not with Head unit server); the picture and sound then travel over Wi-Fi.
Name and password of the car’s own hotspot
CarLink reads them from the car where it can and passes them to your phone. Change them here and CarLink changes the car’s hotspot too, where Android allows it.
This stereo does not let CarLink read its hotspot. Enter the name and password exactly as the car’s hotspot settings show them.
The car’s hotspot now uses this name and password
Saved in CarLink. This stereo does not let CarLink change its hotspot: set the same name and password in the car’s hotspot settings.
The router both the car and your iPhone join
CarPlay only. This screen is on the router by cable (a USB Ethernet adapter); the iPhone still joins the Wi-Fi above.
The car must already be on this Wi-Fi. CarLink tells your iPhone to join it over Bluetooth.
Optional. CarLink finds the phone by itself: first the phone’s hotspot, then the rest of the network.

On the phone, open Android Auto\'s settings, tap Version until developer settings unlock, then choose Start head unit server from the menu. It turns off when the phone restarts. Leave the address empty to find the phone automatically, or type the phone\'s Wi-Fi address (for example 192.168.43.1).
Enter an IPv4 address such as 192.168.1.20
Enter a name of up to 32 characters
Use 8 to 63 characters, or leave it empty for an open network
Review what CarLink is allowed to use
Sharpness and smoothness of the picture
Sharpest, at 60 frames a second. Needs a fast head unit.
Sharp at 30 frames a second. Kind to older head units.
Lower resolution, for slow Wi-Fi or older hardware.
Size of icons and text in CarPlay and Android Auto
For a screen far from the driver
When maps and screens turn dark
Dark between two times you choose
Status-bar hide, accessibility, and the top margin
Is your car a Changan / CS75 Plus 2022-2023?
Hides the car\'s floating notification bar during CarPlay and Android Auto, so it does not cover the picture. Turn it on?
You can change or turn it off any time in Settings. CarLink also needs the Accessibility permission for the hide to work.
The car\'s status bar stays visible.
Hide the status bar in all apps except the home screen
The bar stays visible on the car\'s home/launcher. CarPlay and Android Auto are always hidden in this mode.
Hide the status bar only in apps I pick
Tick apps with ✔. CarPlay and Android Auto are always hidden in this mode, even if CarLink is not ticked.
Notice: You need to turn on the Accessibility permission for CarLink so it can tell which app is open and hide the status bar.
Apps where the bar is hidden
Lets CarLink see which app is in front so it can hide or show the car\'s status bar, as set in Settings for Changan CS75 Plus.

A 48 px space at the top of CarLink, CarPlay and Android Auto, so nothing hides under the car’s status bar. CarLink changes at once, CarPlay and Android Auto from the next connection. Off: no margins.

Hides the car\'s floating status bar while CarPlay or Android Auto is on screen, so it does not sit on top of the projection. Applies at once. Off: the car\'s bar stays visible. This test setting is for the Changan CS75 Plus only.
Saves the app version, device, settings, phone sessions and the full log in one text file: on a USB flash drive if one is in, else Downloads/CarLink. Saved passwords are left out. Works offline.
Sends the same file through another app on this screen
Where music, directions and calls play
The head unit plays all sound. Recommended.
Music goes through the car’s own Bluetooth audio instead.
Smoother picture on a slow screen, with the same sharpness

30 frames per second instead of 60, the picture drawn straight to the screen, and CarLink’s own effects kept simple (when Visual effects is Automatic). The resolution and quality stay the same, so nothing turns pixelated or blurry. Works only when Picture is Automatic.
Default. The picture stays as Picture sets it.
Turns on by itself from the next connection when the picture struggles, and says so. Choose again to reset it.
How far music and video sound is buffered behind the picture
Sound closest to the picture: about 0.1\u00A0s over USB. Wireless stays at 0.3\u00A0s. Try Normal if music stutters.
About 0.3\u00A0s over USB and wireless. Recommended.
Steadiest music on a weak link: about 0.5\u00A0s over USB, 1\u00A0s wireless.
Spoken directions and the voice assistant
CarPlay calls. Android Auto calls go through the car’s Bluetooth hands-free.
Louder or quieter than the phone sends it, for both CarPlay and Android Auto. Above Normal, the loudest peaks are softened so they do not crackle.
How the head unit plays CarPlay calls
Recommended. The head unit treats it as a call and cancels the echo.
For head units that play calls too quietly or not at all. The other person may hear an echo: if so, turn on Call echo cancellation under Show advanced, or go back to Phone call.
If music was playing when the phone disconnected, press play once it is back
Back button goes back in Android Auto
Off: Back opens the menu to leave Android Auto. Either way, swipe in from the left edge with two fingers for that menu.
CarPlay turns its music down while a navigation prompt speaks
How loud your voice reaches calls and the voice assistant
Raise it if people say you sound far away; lower it if you sound distorted. Try it with Test call audio in Diagnostics.
Share the car’s GPS with the phone for steadier directions
Show the next turn on the BYD instrument cluster and head-up display
Keeps CarPlay and Android Auto controls next to the driver
Dark at night, light by day
Car stereo or phone/tablet: CarLink\'s layout and how CarPlay and Android Auto fit the screen
Detects this device. Choose by hand if CarPlay shows black bars or the picture turns when it shouldn\'t
A fixed screen in the car: large controls, the picture never turns
A phone or tablet as the screen: standard sizes, the picture turns with the screen
Light, glow and animation on CarLink’s screens
Simple on this device: little memory or processor power, or Lite mode is on
Soft light, glow, grain and smooth animation
Plain fills and fewer redraws, for slower head units. Same layout and colours
Live picture, sound and link figures for the current session

resources.string: Experimental and debug options, framed in amber
Engine settings for experienced drivers. Changing a picture or size value here sets the matching setting above to Custom.
Experimental and debug options. If a connection stops working, turn them off first.
A small button over CarPlay and Android Auto to switch phones, open CarLink or disconnect
Android needs this before CarLink can show the button
BYD: adds its DiLink extras. Other brands only label this car, except Changan.

Changan: its logo on CarPlay’s back-to-car button (other cars get the default icon). When you pick the CS75 Plus entry you’re asked about hiding the notification bar — in every app except the home screen, or in apps you choose from a full list. The 48 px top-margin test is off by default, and sound plays through the car’s Bluetooth by default. CarPlay still defaults to a 400 mm width and HEVC, and Android Auto to 200 DPI. You can change all of this in Settings.
Pick the make of this car. CarPlay and Android Auto work the same in every car.
Adds a 48 px space at the top of CarPlay, Android Auto and CarLink, so nothing hides under the car’s status bar. Turn it on?
You can turn it off any time in Settings › Display › Top margin.
This screen is not a BYD DiLink unit, so the BYD extras cannot work here. Choose your car\'s make, or Other.
BYD adds the DiLink extras: directions on the HUD and the instrument cluster, and BYD steering-wheel keys.
CarPlay and Android Auto work the same as in any car. The brand only labels this car in CarLink.

CarPlay and Android Auto work as in any car. Changan also shows its logo on CarPlay\'s back-to-car button. Choosing this entry asks about hiding the notification bar, with a full app list if you hide it only in apps you pick. The 48 px top-margin test is off by default, and sound plays through the car’s Bluetooth by default. CarPlay defaults to 400 mm and HEVC, and Android Auto to 200 DPI.
Teach CarLink your wheel\'s buttons for voice, calls and music in CarPlay and Android Auto
Tap Learn, then press the button on the steering wheel. Buttons the stereo keeps for itself never reach CarLink and cannot be learned.
Press a button on the steering wheel…
Volume, Back and Home buttons cannot be used.
No button arrived. The stereo may keep that one for itself.
Permissions, car brand and pairing a phone, step by step

Not supported by Android Auto on this device: Google switches off its car mode on screens it does not support as phones (for example Samsung tablets). It works where Android Auto is installed as a system app, as on many Android head units.

Adds a Home button that runs Android Auto on this device itself, with no phone. Needs Android Auto 17.4 or newer with its head unit server started in Android Auto\'s developer settings; Home shows how.
Save CarLink\'s settings to a file, to restore them later or on another screen
Load settings from a backup file
Anyone who has the file can read it. The car hotspot and Same Wi-Fi passwords are left out unless you include them.
CarLink\'s settings are replaced by the %1$s in this backup. Your phones and their pairing stay as they are.
CarLink\'s settings are replaced by the %1$s in the backup from %2$s. Your phones and their pairing stay as they are.
The backup has no Wi-Fi passwords: the ones saved here are kept.
It is not a CarLink settings backup, or it was changed (%1$s). Nothing was changed.
The language of CarLink and its CarPlay and Android Auto screens
Follows the head unit\'s language, or English if CarLink has no translation for it
Turn on the hotspot in the car settings, then connect your phone to it. If the main settings screen opens, look for the hotspot under network settings.
Could not open settings. Open hotspot settings from the car screen.
